# Known bugs

Open bugs, newest first. IDs (B1, B2, …) are never reused, so commits can say "fixes B1".
A fixed bug is removed in the commit that fixes it, together with a test that reproduces
it: shown failing before the fix and passing after; git history keeps the record. Finding a
bug doesn't mean fixing it at once: it is logged here and its fix scheduled with the user.
Not part of the documentation site.

**Where they live:** one file per bug, `bugs/B<n>.toml` (its title, rating, the date it was
found, whether it is only suspected, and its details in Markdown); this file is
`bugs/README.md`, and `BUGS.md` is generated from them all (`python3 scripts/bugs.py
render`; `make check` fails when it is out of date). A new bug: `python3 scripts/bugs.py new
"<title>"` writes the next number's file, to fill in, and moves `bugs/next-id` on. A fix
deletes the bug's file. The script's docstring shows a file's fields.

A bug found by reasoning but **not reproduced yet** is logged too, marked **Suspected**, with
how it would be confirmed; once a test shows it, the mark goes. If it turns out not to be a
bug, the entry is removed, saying why in the commit.


## Ratings

Every bug has three ratings, set when it is logged (by whoever finds it; Claude checks them)
and revised when more is known:

- **Severity**, what happens when it occurs: **critical** (a security hole, silent wrong
  results or wrong code run, a task run twice, the whole cluster stuck); **high** (in normal
  operation, with no mistake by the DAG's author, a task or run fails wrongly, stalls, runs on
  after a cancel, or a worker can't work); **medium** (a visible, repeatable failure that
  testing a DAG would catch, slowness growing with scale, a misleading UI or CLI); **low**
  (cosmetic, a message, a test-only flake, an author's type mistake caught at run time
  instead of at load).
- **Probability**, in a real deployment: **likely** (ordinary use or routine events),
  **possible** (a specific but plausible situation: a reconnect at the wrong moment, git-sync,
  a feature combination, scale), **rare** (unusual input, exact timing, extreme sizes, a
  hostile actor). For a security bug: how easily it is triggered, by accident or on purpose.
- **Kind**: security, data, correctness, reliability, performance, usability or tests.
  Security is a kind, not a third score: its worst case is already the severity.

**Score** = severity (critical 4, high 3, medium 2, low 1) × probability (likely 3,
possible 2, rare 1). The ranking below puts **every security bug first**, whatever its score
(the user, 2026-10-30), then the rest by score, then severity; fixes go in its order
unless the user schedules otherwise. The score is computed by the script, never written by
hand; each entry's first line in `BUGS.md` is its rating.

**What gets fixed when** (the user, 2026-10-30): every bug of severity **high or critical** is
fixed (security first, then the ranking), then features go on; a new high or critical bug
interrupts the feature work and is fixed next. Medium and low bugs wait here, fixed when a
step touches their code or the user schedules them.

## B214: `dags test` drops the warning for a `--for` without an offset

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **likely**, usability (score 3): `--for` and `--event-at` are parsed with `parse_for` and only `.at` is kept: the documented warning that an offset-free time is read as UTC is never shown.
- **Found:** 2026-11-10, by Codex's full review (F12b), each with a probe failing on the code.
- **Where:** `crates/schedr/src/local.rs` (`.map(|t| t.at)` for both).
- **Shown:** Codex's probe: `--for 2026-01-01T12:00:00`, exit 0, no warning.
- **A fix:** print the `ParsedTime`'s warning on stderr, as `runs trigger` does.

## B213: `tasks logs --follow` never ends for a task that will get no attempt

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **possible**, usability (score 4): with no attempt yet, following waits and polls for ever without looking at the task's or run's state: an `upstream_failed` task's log follow never returns.
- **Found:** 2026-11-10, by Codex's full review (F12b), each with a probe failing on the code.
- **Where:** `crates/schedr/src/user.rs` (`(None, None) if args.follow => {}`).
- **Shown:** Codex's probe on a real standalone: run failed, task `upstream_failed`, no attempts; the follow didn't exit.
- **A fix:** stop following once the task is in an end state without attempts (or the run has ended), saying so.

## B212: a configuration with Basic sign-in makes `dags test` fail on its own server

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **possible**, correctness (score 4): the test's temporary webserver keeps `[webserver.auth]` while its own client always calls with no sign-in: `error: not signed in`, and `--user` doesn't reach that client.
- **Found:** 2026-11-10, by Codex's full review (F12b), each with a probe failing on the code.
- **Where:** `crates/schedr/src/local.rs` (`HttpTransport::new(api, Auth::None)` against a server with `config.webserver.auth`).
- **Shown:** Codex's probe with `mode = "basic"`, `--user anna`, `SCHEDR_PASSWORD`: exit 1, `not signed in`.
- **A fix:** the local server runs with sign-in off (it listens on 127.0.0.1 for this run only).

## B205: the chart turns `-` into `_` in interpreter and root names, the loader keeps them

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **possible**, correctness (score 4): `upper | replace "-" "_"` in the chart's env names, while the loader only lowercases: `config.DAGS__INTERPRETER: etl-venv` with the fork server on fails at start; `dagsRoot: etl-jobs` silently becomes `etl_jobs`.
- **Found:** 2026-11-10, by Codex's full review (F12a), each with a probe failing on the code.
- **Where:** `charts/schedr/templates/_helpers.tpl` (`schedr.forkServerEnv`), `charts/schedr/templates/_dags.tpl`, `crates/schedr-config/src/sources.rs` `env_key`. Contradicts `docs/03-guide/10-deployment.md` (lines 86-88). Shown by loading the variables the templates produce; helm itself not run.
- **A fix:** refuse names with `-` in those chart values (fail with a message), or pass such tables as one JSON value instead of keyed variables.

## B199: a backfill over a daylight-saving change of a sub-minute cron holds the master up

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **rare**, performance (score 2): each fire time near an offset change walks hours of wall-clock matches; a 1000-run backfill (or its dry run) of a per-second cron over one blocks the master core for minutes.
- **Found:** 2026-11-09, by Codex's review of M4.12b, measured: a dry run of
  `Cron("* * * * * *", tz="Europe/Warsaw")` from `2026-10-25T00:59:00Z` to `01:15:39Z`
  (1000 fire times) took 119 s in a debug build (12 ms in UTC). `fire_times_in`
  (`crates/schedr-master/src/scheduler/backfill.rs`) calls `FireTimes::next_after` per fire
  time; near an offset change `walk_after` (`crates/schedr-master/src/fire_times.rs`) walks
  every match from `MARGIN` (3 h) before the moment, about 21600 for a per-second cron, under
  the core's lock. A per-minute cron walks about 360 per lookup: fine.
- **A fix:** enumerate a range's fire times in one walk (`FireTimes::between`: every match
  from `from - MARGIN` to `to + MARGIN`, their moments by the same rules, sorted, deduped,
  stopping past `max`), so the work is the range's matches, not matches times fire times.

## B196: a bad body's error would show an unknown enum value (unknown variant `…`) (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, security (score 1): body_error hides quoted values and those serde backticks after integer, floating point, boolean and character; serde's unknown variant `x` names the sent value in backticks too, so a request body that gains an enum field would echo it.
- **Found:** a side agent reading B194's fix (b1f3d25, `crates/schedr-api/src/routes.rs`,
  `without_values`, `BACKTICKED_VALUES`). Not reachable today: no request body read through
  `body_error` (TriggerRequest, PauseRequest, CheckConnectionsRequest, TestConnectionRequest,
  PostEventRequest) has an enum field; checked by Claude.
- **The design:** D134: bad bodies produce no value-bearing diagnostics.
- **Fix proposed:** in the next review round of B194's fix: a test with a body whose field is an
  enum given an unknown value, then hide the backticked value after `unknown variant ` too (keeping
  the expected variants serde lists, which are names, not values).

## B195: a moved cleanup's take-back checks the worker it last moved from, not its origin (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): D308: an unassigned move is adopted back by the returning original worker; the take-back (core.rs, attempts.rs) compares only moved_from, so after two moves a worker the cleanup passed through, not its origin, could take it back; whether that can happen is not shown yet.
- **Found:** a Sonnet agent checking D308's summary; not confirmed by Claude: the take-back in
  `crates/schedr-master/src/core.rs` (around 1505) and `crates/schedr-db/src/attempts.rs`
  (around 610) checks `moved_from == worker`; only `rest_owed_by` uses `cleanup_origin`.
- **The design:** D308: the returning worker cleans handles the master never received.
- **Next:** decide whether a second move keeps `moved_from` at the origin; if not, a test with a
  cleanup moved twice, then compare with `cleanup_origin`.

## B193: a DAG in an ID conflict still has its queued tasks assigned (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 2): The design says that while a DAG ID is in conflict no tasks are assigned and tasks not yet started wait until it is resolved; ready_instances doesn't look at dags.conflict, so a conflicting DAG's runs in progress go on assigning tasks.
- **Found:** Grok writing `design/code-delivery.md`; checked by Claude by reading the code, not
  reproduced yet: `ready_instances` (`crates/schedr-db/src/attempts.rs`) filters on the task's
  and run's states only; the conflict stops new runs (`runs.rs`: `conflict IS NULL` when
  triggering) but not assignment.
- **The design:** `archive/PROJECT.md`, DAG ID conflicts: "no new runs are created and no tasks are
  assigned ... tasks not yet started wait until the conflict is resolved" (decision 107).
- **Fix proposed:** skip a conflicting DAG's queued tasks in `ready_instances` (they stay queued
  with the reason, "waiting: DAG ID conflict"), assigned again once the conflict is resolved; a
  test with two files defining one DAG ID while a run has a queued task.

## B192: a removed DAG's queued tasks are still dispatched, not cancelled (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **possible**, correctness (score 4): The design says a removed DAG's runs finish their running attempts and cancel tasks not started; removal only sets dags.removed_at, and ready_instances keeps assigning the runs' queued tasks, which run on a worker still on the run's code and fail elsewhere as dag_file_missing.
- **Found:** Grok writing `design/code-delivery.md` (the docs restructuring); checked by Claude by
  reading the code, not reproduced yet: `DagChange::Remove` (`crates/schedr-db/src/dags.rs`) runs
  only `UPDATE dags SET removed_at = ...` and forgets the trigger's passed events;
  `ready_instances` (`crates/schedr-db/src/attempts.rs`) selects queued tasks of running runs with
  no look at the DAG's removal. `dispatch/tests.rs` shows such a task failing on newer code ("DAG
  `sync` was removed ... after this run started"), so it fails or runs depending on the worker.
- **The design:** `archive/PROJECT.md`, DAG code delivery, "Runs in progress: attempts already
  running finish; tasks not started yet are cancelled".
- **Fix proposed:** on removal, cancel the DAG's running runs' tasks not started (as a cancel
  command would, cleanups still running), in the same transaction; a test removing a DAG with a
  queued task and a running one.

## B191: a worker's Finished that failed to store still wakes the master's loop

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): Decision 42 wakes the loop for a Finished once recorded; the stream reader notifies for any Finished in the turn, also one whose handling failed, so a failed store costs an extra round (rate-limited by ROUND_GAP).
- **Found:** Codex's step round of the docs restructuring (D42/D43 against the code); checked by
  Claude in `crates/schedr-master/src/service.rs`: `finished |= matches!(message, Finished(_))` is
  set before `self.handle(...)`, and `self.finished.notify_one()` runs after the loop whatever the
  handling's result (a data fault drops the message; another error ends the stream).
- **Effect:** one extra scheduler round, at least `ROUND_GAP` after the last; nothing is dispatched
  wrongly, since the round reads the stored state.
- **Fix proposed:** set `finished` only when `handle` returned `Ok` for a `Finished`; a unit test
  with a refused `Finished` and no wake.

## B187: a 0.1 worker given a DAG with fields added since 0.1.0 runs it without them, as the protocol's minor version wasn't raised

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **possible**, correctness (score 4): TaskKind has no deny_unknown_fields and both ends are protocol 0.1: a worker of 0.1.0 under a newer master (the supported upgrade order) drops what it doesn't know, e.g. batch_ms, and runs a batched poke as one event per item, the run's data then not the list its tasks take.
- **Found:** Grok's security review of M4.11f, by parsing DAG JSON with the fields of 0.1.0
  (`batch_ms` dropped, the runner then telling one event per item).
- **Cause:** `PROTOCOL_VERSION` is still 0.1, raised for nothing added in M4 (14 changes to the
  proto since v0.1.0); the master assigns to any worker of an equal or lower minor; the model's
  task JSON ignores fields it doesn't know.
- **Fix proposed:** raise the protocol's minor at the next release, and have the master assign a
  task, trigger or wait step using a newer feature only to workers of that minor or later (or
  refuse such a DAG while an older worker serves its queue); a test with a worker saying 0.1.

## B185: an @sensor(wait_for=EventNamed) that returned NOT_YET never sees an event committed late with an earlier posted_at

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 2): Two posts of one name and key overlap, the later-timed one commits first and is handed to the sensor, which returns NOT_YET; the earlier-timed one, committed after, is behind the sensor's cursor and is never given to it.
- **Found:** Grok's security review of M4.11e part 2, with a throwaway dispatch test
  (`a_sensor_not_yet_still_sees_an_event_committed_late_with_an_earlier_posted_at`, failing:
  0 handed where 1 was expected; removed).
- **Cause:** `NOT_YET` keeps the handed event as `waited_*` (`run_of.rs`), and the next search
  (`first_named_event`) takes only events strictly after that `(posted_at, id)`. A post's time
  is taken before its commit, so one committed late can sit behind the cursor. The trigger form
  reads back a minute (`SCHEDR_HIDDEN__MASTER__EVENT_LOOKBACK`) and skips what it passed
  (`trigger_passed`); the sensor has no such lookback.
- **Fix proposed:** the same as the trigger's: read back the lookback behind the cursor and skip
  the events this wait step was already given (kept per instance, as `trigger_passed` is per
  DAG). A test posts two overlapping events, the later committed first.

## B184: 500 wait steps ending at once take about 23 s to be recorded, about 22 a second

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **possible**, performance (score 4): Stress scenario 23 (`23_many_sensors`): 500 wait steps on one worker, released together by a file; each awaiting `@sensor` checks every 1 s, yet their ends spread evenly over 0 to 23 s after the file (p50 10.6 s, p99 22.6 s), and the pokes (every 5 s) come later still (p50 24 s, p99 35 s). A throughput limit on a burst of ends, somewhere between the watcher host, the agent and the master's recording.
- **Found:** 2026-11-08, `make stress STRESS=23_many_sensors` (quick profile) on the M4.11d2
  part 2 tree: all 500 succeed; memory is fine (about 135 KiB a wait step, one host at 41 MiB).
- **To find:** where the time goes when many wait steps end in the same second: the host's
  results sent one by one, the agent forwarding them, or the master recording each `Finished`
  (attempt, output, instance, and a run when its last step ends) in transactions of its own.
  One step noticing a change alone is fast.
- **Cause (Grok's investigation, 2026-11-08; checked against `core.rs`):** the master. Each
  `Started` and each `Finished` is its own `db.atomically` (`MasterCore::finished`, and the
  `Started` arm of `handle`): on file SQLite about 15 ms each (an 8 ms durable commit plus the
  statements), so a burst records at about 67 a second alone and 53 in `schedr standalone`, the
  `Finished`s queued behind the `Started`s still committing. The host sends the burst at about
  1400 a second and the agent's journal writes one in about 5 ms: neither is the limit.
  Postgres (the stress run's 22 a second) not measured.
- **Postponed to M4B** (the user, 2026-11-08): batching the whole turn's messages is M4B's
  work anyway.
- **Fix proposed (for M4B):** the messages of one worker's turn (`MESSAGES_PER_TURN`, 10) that
  are `Finished` (and a leading run of `Started`) committed in one transaction, ending the batch at
  any other message so the order holds; a data fault taken out of it and stored on its own (B106);
  a failed commit stores and acks none (the journal resends); `CommitUnknown` settles every
  attempt of the batch. A test counts the write transactions (`count_writes`): today one per
  message, then about one per ten.
- **Why it matters:** a sensor's point is reacting soon; a burst of events (a shared file, a
  run many steps wait for) delays the last by tens of seconds.
- **To be fixed in M4B** (decisions 395, D396, the user, 2026-11-09): a turn in one transaction,
  its `Finished`s written together, each run settled once per turn, the agent's journal in groups
  (M4B.4, M4B.5); fixed when stress 23 records its 500 ends within 5 s on Postgres.

## B166: Stress scenario 15's round-time ratio went over its limit in CI (1.167 > 1.15)

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **possible**, tests (score 2): The nightly Stress run on 2026-11-05 (run 42003419375, on b9fa0e3) failed only scenario 15 (`15_change_signals`): the master's mean round with the change triggers on was 1.167 times the one without, over the 1.15 limit; a noisy comparison on a shared CI runner, or a real cost of the triggers.
- **Found:** 2026-11-05, the scheduled Stress run 42003419375 (`round_mean_ratio = 1.167, over
  its limit 1.15`, crates/schedr/tests/stress/check.rs:465). The run before passed (11-04); runs
  on 10-31 to 11-02 failed (not checked here which scenario).
- **To check:** the ratio over the last runs' reports (the JSON artefacts), and whether it
  moves with the runner's load; then either a wider limit or more samples (a noisy comparison),
  or the triggers' cost looked at (a real regression).
- **Why it matters:** a red nightly hides real failures; the triggers' cost is what scenario 15
  exists to bound.

## B161: A task's log showed `No` masked in a client's error, matching no secret (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): The demo's MySQL client task logged `...caching_sha2_password.so: **** such file or directory`: `No` masked, though none of the attempt's secrets (`dev_app`, a 24-character password, `dev`, too short to mask) is `No`; the mask set alone doesn't reproduce it.
- **Found:** 2026-11-03, running the connections demo (M4.7d): `mysql_from_its_client`, its
  connection `orders_db` as `MY` (the MySQL option file), the client failing for a missing
  plugin; read with `schedr tasks logs`.
- **Not reproduced:** a `MaskSet` (min 5) holding the attempt's values masks nothing in the
  exact line (`mask_text` and `mask`). Left to check: the stream masking across chunks
  (the client's stderr written in pieces), the derived forms (`cnf_escaped`), the values of
  the other declared secrets, and whether the reader (`tasks logs`) masks again.
- **Why it matters:** over-masking makes a log mislead (an error reads as a secret); not a
  leak.

## B159: A registration test with many new roots timed out its 10 s wait under `make check`'s load

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **possible**, tests (score 2): `schedr-master`'s `a_registration_with_more_new_roots_than_a_stream_holds_gets_every_parse` (B45's test) takes 4.3-4.8 s alone, and its registration has 10 s to answer: in a full `make check` (2008 tests, the machine busy) it ran out once, `registered in time: Elapsed(())` at `crates/schedr-master/src/service/tests.rs:1557`.
- **Found:** 2026-11-03, by Claude, in M4.7b1's `make check` (1921 of 2008 passed, this one
  failed); alone it passed five times in five, at 4.3-4.8 s. M4.7b1 doesn't touch
  registration.
- **When:** possible: the whole Rust suite running in parallel on a busy machine (WSL).
- **A fix:** find where its 4.5 s go (a parse per root, `STREAM_BUFFER + 10` roots, each
  probably a real runner) and make that cheaper, or wait on progress (each `Registered` or
  parse message) rather than one 10 s limit for the whole registration.

## B157: Inputs just under the inline limit push an assignment past the worker's 4 MiB message (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **rare**, reliability (score 2): `AssignTask` keeps inputs inline up to `INLINE_INPUTS_LIMIT` (4 MiB), the worker's whole gRPC message limit; the task's JSON, its run's params and its connections come on top, so inputs of a little under 4 MiB make a message the worker can't decode: its control stream ends, the task is never started and goes back to the queue after the start timeout, again and again.
- **Found:** 2026-11-03, by Claude checking Grok's M4.7a security finding (a root's whole
  connection registry rode in each assignment; fixed there: only the task's declared ones go).
  Read in `crates/schedr-master/src/dispatch.rs`: `external = inputs.len() >
  INLINE_INPUTS_LIMIT`, with `INLINE_INPUTS_LIMIT = 4 * 1024 * 1024`; the worker's
  `MasterClient` keeps tonic's default 4 MiB receive limit (`crates/schedr/src/roles.rs`,
  which `schedr-config`'s `MIN_MESSAGE_SIZE` says workers rely on). Not reproduced yet.
- **When:** rare: an upstream output of a little under 4 MiB passed whole to a task.
- **A fix:** the inline decision on the whole message's encoded size (inputs, task JSON,
  params, connections) with a margin, e.g. inputs inline only while the message stays under
  4 MiB less 64 KiB; a test with inputs of 4 MiB less a few bytes.

## B156: An action's status stops being followed after an error answer

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **possible**, usability (score 2): the UI's pending-command note replaces itself with whatever its poll gets: an HTTP error (a proxy's 502 while the UI restarts, a lapsed sign-in's 401) ends the following, the note showing the error page.
- **Found:** 2026-11-03, by Grok reviewing M4.6f (the log tail had the same shape, fixed
  there); confirmed by Claude reading `crates/schedr-ui/templates/command.html`: the note polls
  itself (`hx-trigger="load delay:…"`, `hx-swap="outerHTML"`), htmx swaps every status but 204
  (`templates/base.html`'s `responseHandling`), and neither the live parts' guard nor the log
  tail's retry covers it.
- **When:** possible: an action is sent while the UI restarts behind a proxy, or as a sign-in
  lapses; the master still decides the command, only the page stops saying so.
- **A fix:** as the log tail's: an error answer isn't swapped in; the poll is asked again a
  second later (a `retry` trigger on the note).

## B154: The scheduler's skipped DAGs are never logged

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, reliability (score 1): a DAG whose fire times or default params fail in a scheduler pass creates no run, and nothing says why.
- **Found:** 2026-11-01, by Grok writing the params docs; confirmed by Claude: `Pass.skipped`
  (`crates/schedr-master/src/scheduler.rs`) gets `SchedulerError::FireTimes` and, since M4.5a,
  `SchedulerError::Params` (a scheduled run's defaults refused), but nothing in the master reads
  it.
- **When:** rare: both are checked when the DAG is validated, so it takes a master whose checks
  changed after the DAG was stored (an upgrade), or a bug in them.
- **A fix:** log each skipped DAG once (warn) with the reason, and perhaps show it as the DAG's
  problem, as a hold is shown.

## B153: A `Literal` field can't be rendered into a command's t-string

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **possible**, usability (score 2): `t"{dag_ctx.params.region}"` with `region: Literal["eu", "us"]` is refused at parse time, though its values are text.
- **Found:** 2026-11-01, by Grok writing the params docs: archive/PROJECT.md's own example
  (`region: Literal["eu", "us"]` in `t"{dag_ctx.params.region}"`) fails to import with
  ``a value of type `Literal['eu', 'us']` can't be rendered into text``.
- **Cause:** `python/schedr/_build.py` `is_renderable` takes scalars, `Any`, unions of them and
  a model's scalar field; a `LiteralType` is none of these. The same holds for a task output
  typed `Literal[...]`.
- **A fix:** a `Literal` whose values are all text, numbers or booleans is renderable (the agent
  renders the stored JSON scalar); check the agent's render of such a value, and a format spec
  on it.

## B152: `rm -rf .schedr`, which the guide gives to start afresh, fails on the code store

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **likely**, usability (score 3): the worker's code copies are read-only directories: `rm -rf` can't delete their files.
- **Found:** 2026-11-01, by Claude, deleting a `make standalone-separate-ui` data directory:
  `rm: cannot remove '…/code/localhost/examples-c590b3c9/sha256-…/sync.py': Permission
  denied`, for every file of every copy.
- **Cause:** the code store makes each copy's directories read-only (`dr-xr-xr-x`), so a task
  can't change the code it runs (decision 101). Deleting a file needs its directory writable.
- **Affected:** the guide's "`rm -rf .schedr` starts afresh" (`make standalone`, Deployment),
  and anyone deleting a worker's `data_dir` by hand.
- **A fix:** say `chmod -R u+w .schedr && rm -rf .schedr` (or a `make standalone-clean`
  target doing it), or find what the store could do instead.

## B151: standalone once didn't exit after its master was taken over (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, reliability (score 1): `standalone_ends_when_its_master_is_taken_over` failed once in `make check` (2026-11-01, check18): the master logged "the master failed: standalone stops", then nothing for 20 s, and the process didn't exit. A standalone left running so would serve its API and worker with no master, never restarted.
- **Found:** check18, during the bug batch B135-B138/B147 (`FAIL [41.139s]`). Passes alone (4 of 4, 15 s each).
- **Where to look:** after the master fails, `request` 2 stops the worker, whose end sends `stop` to the API (`standalone.rs`); something there didn't end: the worker's interrupt, the API's open streams (the client's stream tasks changed for B138 in that batch), or the ops server.
- **Bounded (2026-11-01):** once the master failed, standalone gives its worker
  `WORKER_STOP_AFTER_FAILURE` (10 s) to stop, then stops anyway, logging "the worker didn't
  stop within 10s of the master's failure" (`standalone::ended_within`, unit-tested on paused
  time). So the process exits; the cause is not found (not reproduced: the agent's awaits
  outside its select (`hashes()` while a root settles, `client.control()` opening the stream)
  are the candidates). Lowered to low: what is left is a slower exit, and the log line to
  find the cause the next time it happens.

## B150: A failed migration's lease stayed held once under the coverage run (flaky test) (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, tests (score 1): `roles::tests::a_failed_migration_gives_the_lease_back` failed once in `make check` (coverage, heavy load: neighbouring tests took 7 s instead of 0.1 s): the lease was still held after `schedr db migrate` failed. Likely the release query hit its 5 s limit (logged, the lease then expires by itself after its period).
- **Found:** check13 during M4.4b (`FAIL [7.503s]`, "the lease stayed held"). Not reproduced: 5 runs alone, 3 runs of the schedr lib tests, 48 copies at once all passed.
- **Suspected cause:** `migrate_holding` releases on the query-limited database; the failed migration's connection is closed on drop in the background (`Starting::drop`, `close_on_drop`), so its SQLite write lock may outlive the error and the release waits on it, past the limit when the machine is loaded.
- **A fix:** close the failed migration's connection (awaited) before giving the lease back; or retry the release once. The test could also capture the warning to tell the two apart.

## B148: the limit check searches a DAG's task list for each ready task, every round

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **rare**, performance (score 2): with thousands of ready tasks in one DAG under a task limit, each round looks every one up twice in the DAG's task list (`Dag::task` is a linear search): quadratic work under the master's lock.
- **Found:** 2026-11-01, by Codex's review of M4.4 (finding 3), measured in a debug build: limit checks alone took 25 ms for 1,000 ready tasks, 379 ms for 4,000, 2.1 s for 8,000. `crates/schedr-master/src/limits.rs` (`Active::reached`).
- **Done meanwhile:** the DAG's `max_active_tasks` is checked first, with no lookup; once it is reached, every ready task of the DAG is held back without a search. What remains is a DAG under its cap with many ready tasks that have their own limits.
- **A fix:** look the task up once (`assign_one` already has it) and pass its settings in, or index a DAG's tasks by ID when its version is read.

## B89: a run whose stored DAG no longer reads looks unmapped to the API

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): a mapped task's instances refused as unmapped and a missing task given an empty list; a stored DAG JSON that no longer deserializes (a field the model lost).
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Grok's follow-up review of M4.3d (`324d99d5`), with a probe that
  added an unknown field to a run's `dag_versions.dag_json` (`Dag` is `deny_unknown_fields`).
  `run_tasks` (`crates/schedr-api/src/routes.rs`) turns the serde error into `None` (`.ok()`),
  so `mapped_count` treats every task as unmapped and known: a missing task's attempts are
  200 `{"attempts": []}`, `?map_index=0` on a mapped task is a 400 "isn't mapped", `retry`
  without an index is accepted; `get_run` shows the whole task's `instances` as null. A
  value that isn't JSON at all is a 500. The earlier `mapped_tasks` behaved the same.
- **A fix:** a DAG that doesn't read is the API's error (a 500 naming the run), not an
  unmapped DAG; or keep reading it leniently for `get_run` only. Before 1.0.0 the stored
  JSON follows the model (edited in place); after it, migrations must keep it readable.

## B85: disconnects during notification draining can silently lose changes

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 2): the UI's live feed misses changes until the next one; the database listener disconnecting with a notification queued.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F4 (the database layer),
  medium severity, confirmed by Codex's failing test, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `crates/schedr-db/src/changes.rs:220`. Only the first receive handles `None` as `Change::Missed`. The subsequent drain accepts only notifications: This discards a disconnect result or cancels reconnection after the listener has consumed its disconnect state. **Scenario:** one notification is queued → the listening connection dies → another change occurs while disconnected → draining consumes the disconnect → following resumes without reporting `Missed`. The API feed sends a refresh for `Missed` (`schedr-api/src/events.rs:122`), so clients can retain stale data. **
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B82: settling can perform cubic work on a chain

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **rare**, performance (score 2): the master's lock held for seconds; a long chain listed in reverse order.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F3 (runs moving forward),
  medium severity, confirmed by Codex's failing test, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `crates/schedr-master/src/progress.rs:454`. Each pass visits all tasks and calls `edges_into()` for scheduled tasks. That helper scans the entire edge vector (`crates/schedr-model/src/dag.rs:116`): The outer loop repeats until nothing changes. A chain listed in reverse dependency order advances one task per pass, yielding Θ(T²E) work—Θ(T³) for a chain. **Scenario:** preparing an 800-task empty chain occupies the master’s core lock for seconds; the service holds that lock while ticking. Batch measurement `f3_settle_scaling`, unoptimized test build: Both task orders produced the same successful result. The same edge-scanning helper is used in mapped settling at `progress.rs:554` and `:600`. **Confidence: high for the complexity; measured timings are debug-build figures.**
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B77: valid large timedeltas cannot render in agent templates

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): a timedelta beyond ~292,000 years can't be rendered into a command.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F8 (the Python runner
  and serialization), low severity, with a failing check; Codex's check, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `python/schedr/_serialization/codec.py:159`. Python stores the full supported timedelta range as integer microseconds. Agent rendering accepts the tag only through `Value::as_i64` at `crates/schedr-agent/src/render.rs:261`. `timedelta(days=200000000)` encodes successfully and its microsecond count survives the channel exactly, but rendering treats it as an unsupported object.
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B74: `Literal` compatibility conflates booleans with integers

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): `Literal[True]` accepted for `Literal[1]` at load, failing at run time.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F8 (the Python runner
  and serialization), medium severity, with a failing check; Codex's check, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `python/schedr/_serialization/compatibility.py:151`. The check uses `v in target.values`, so Python equality makes `True` fit `1`. The runtime Literal codec requires both equal value and equal type. A `Literal[True]` producer therefore connects successfully to a `Literal[1]` parameter, then fails at execution.
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B73: optional TypedDict keys are falsely promised as present

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): an optional nested TypedDict key accepted as required at load.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F8 (the Python runner
  and serialization), medium severity, with a failing check; Codex's check, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `python/schedr/_serialization/models.py:105`. `_all_required()` sets `copied["required"] = list(node["properties"])` on every nested object schema. A model’s nested TypedDict can legitimately omit `NotRequired` keys; dumping the model does not add them. A model containing `row: {x: NotRequired[int]}` is consequently accepted for one requiring `row.x`.
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B72: approximate divisibility admits incompatible `multipleOf` constraints

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): huge `multipleOf` constraints compared approximately at load.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F8 (the Python runner
  and serialization), medium severity, with a failing check; Codex's check, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `python/schedr/_serialization/schemas.py:538`. The proof uses `math.isclose(ratio, round(ratio))`. Its relative tolerance accepts nonintegral ratios at sufficiently large magnitudes. A source with `multiple_of=10**12` is accepted for a target with `multiple_of=3`, although `10**12` itself fails that target.
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B71: integer constraint comparisons lose precision

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): integer bounds above 2^53 compared as floats at load.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F8 (the Python runner
  and serialization), medium severity, with a failing check; Codex's check, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `python/schedr/_serialization/schemas.py:517`. `_limit()` converts integer boundaries with `float(schema[plain])`. This collapses distinct boundaries above the exact integer range of a float. A source allowing `x >= 9007199254740992` is accepted for a target requiring `x >= 9007199254740993`. The source’s minimum value then fails decoding.
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B70: reference memoization skips comparisons against different inline target schemas

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, correctness (score 1): one reference compared against two different inline targets, cached as one.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F8 (the Python runner
  and serialization), medium severity, with a failing check; Codex's check, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `python/schedr/_serialization/schemas.py:246`. The cache key contains only reference strings:
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B69: embedding a model descriptor loses its `$ref` resolution context

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **possible**, correctness (score 2): a wrong `list[Model]` connection accepted at load, failing at run time.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F8 (the Python runner
  and serialization), medium severity, with a failing check; Codex's check, not yet re-checked by Claude; at `python/schedr/_serialization/schemas.py:132`. `from_desc()` nests a model’s schema and `$defs` under `items` or another enclosing schema. `_Compare` continues resolving references from the outer root. At `schemas.py:444`, a missing definition becomes `{}`, which `fits()` accepts as unrestricted. Thus `list[TextBox]`, containing a model field `x: str`, is accepted for `list[IntBox]`, whose corresponding field is `x: int`. The same comparison without the enclosing list correctly rejects it.
- **A fix:** to decide when it is scheduled.

## B48: every attempt message copies the master's whole worker registry under its lock

- **Rating:** severity **medium**, probability **rare**, performance (score 2): each worker message costs in proportion to the whole registry; hundreds of workers.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Codex's whole-repository review, section F1 (the master's core
  loop and the worker link), with a failing proof each; checked against the code by Claude.
  `Started`, `Rejected` and `Finished` each take `Dispatcher::memory` (the D1 snapshot: `workers`, `rejections`, `code_missing` cloned, `crates/schedr-master/src/core.rs:499`, `dispatch.rs:280`) under the core lock, so each message costs in proportion to the whole registry and its outstanding attempts; Codex measured 10 vs 1,000 workers (4 attempts each), 500 snapshots each, unrelated attempts included.
- **A fix:** a snapshot of what the message can change (its attempt and worker) instead of everything; measure first with M4B.1's per-turn timings.

## B40: a lease test times out its 2 s query limit under load

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **likely**, tests (score 3): a lease test fails under load.
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, in `make check` while two other builds and test runs shared the
  machine: `lease::tests::a_master_taken_over_never_writes_itself_back_as_the_holder` failed
  with `QueryTimeout(2s)` (`crates/schedr-master/src/lease/tests.rs:101`, an `unwrap` on a
  query). Alone it passed 5 times out of 5 (6-9 s each).
- **The cause, likely:** the test runs with the production 2 s query limit; SQLite under a
  loaded CPU can exceed it. Not investigated: whether the test exercises a write that should
  be retried rather than a limit that should be longer in tests.
- **Seen again:** 2026-10-30, `make check` while a worktree's full build ran:
  `schedr-db` `scope::tests::a_masters_work_is_refused_once_its_lease_was_taken_over`
  (`QueryTimeout(2s)`), `scope::tests::work_that_fails_stores_nothing` (`QueryTimeout(4s)`)
  and `query::tests::an_sqlite_write_waits_for_another_writer_instead_of_failing` (SQLite's
  "database is locked"); all three use the production limits.
- **A fix:** the test's own query limit (or a retry of what the master retries itself), and
  the same check over the other tests using the default limit.

## B39: sibling groups on different layers make the run graph far too wide (partly fixed; the rest after 1.0.0, in M6)

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **possible**, usability (score 2): DAGs with many groups drawn far too wide (M6).
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Grok's review of M4.2b's graph layout (decision 65). A group was
  moved only on the layers holding its tasks while its box covers every layer between, so
  boxes stretched and pushed the next group further each pass: 8 sibling groups of 3 tasks
  reached tens of thousands of px.
- **Partly fixed, merged 2026-10-30** (Grok sessions `e9ee40d3`, `3b1e9c47`, reviewed by Codex
  `01a18cef`; the user merged it after a comparison with the earlier layout on 3,000 random
  grouped DAGs: 1,669 narrower by over 10%, 1,192 about the same, **139 wider** by over 10%
  (up to 2.7x, 6,000-14,000 px); the widest from 51,250 to 13,963 px; 8 / 16 flat staggered
  groups from 29,987 / 7,145,763 px to 2,992 / 5,825; layout time about the same).
  Decisions with the user,
  1 A (a group is a rigid column: its layers share the rightmost left edge, moving only right;
  a pushed item takes its outermost group along, on every layer, each item once), 5 A
  (outermost first), 7 A (a nested group whose layers don't line up is its own column; its
  parent doesn't drag a layer holding it); tests 2 A, 3 A (random trees of 1-6 groups, a
  4-deep nest, a group skipping layers), 8 B (one extra row in the random width bound). The
  original shape is fixed (8 groups: 29,987 px before, now within the side-by-side bound).
- **Open (Codex's review), for M6:** the 139 random shapes the merged layout draws wider; R1
  (high) nested staggered siblings still grow about 4x per doubling (16 parents 27,169 px, 32:
  100,629, against 7.4 million and 4.6e11 px before); R2 quadratic scans per round (`take_group`,
  `align_group`, `shift_closure`, `clear`); R3 a transitive push moves only the innermost
  group; R4 the random properties pass when no box is drawn. **Chosen, not implemented:**
  9 A (pull a nested group left of its parent's column onto it, indented; don't chase one to
  the right; push by the largest single intrusion, always the outermost group), 10 A (one
  work counter over the four scans, bound 8n), 11 A (the seven-task R3 graph), 12 B (every
  populated group has a box, plus a populated-and-empty fixed test).
- **Seen again, 2026-10-31:** `grouped_nodes_never_overlap_and_fit` found a random 13-node,
  two-deep grouping 5,830 px wide against the bound's 5,612 (seed saved in
  `crates/schedr-ui/proptest-regressions/graph/tests.txt`); the test bound now has 10% more
  room (the user), the shape stays replayed, the layout itself waits for M6.
- **Parked** (the user, 2026-10-30): back in M6, as a layout correct by construction (each
  group a block, placed recursively) plus a safety net (check, then fall back to strips),
  PLAN.md M6. It affects only how DAGs with many groups are drawn, nothing that runs; each
  review round of the repair approach found the next shape.

## B38: an edge between two tasks outside a group can be drawn through its box

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **possible**, usability (score 2): an edge drawn through a group's box (M6).
- **Found:** 2026-10-30, by Grok's review of M4.2b's graph layout. On a layer a group spans
  without a task there, a task outside it is pushed right of the box on that layer only;
  the edge from it to a task on the other side is a curve between the two, through the box.
  Decision 65 keeps tasks out of boxes, not lines. Grok's case: `A0 -> U -> A1`, `U -> B1`,
  `A = {A0, A1}`, `B = {B0, B1}`: `U` lands right of `B`, its edges cross `B`'s box.
- **Cosmetic:** every task is in the right box. **A fix:** route such edges around boxes,
  or order layers so that it can't happen; with B39.

## B24: a forked attempt started while the master link is down is recorded as `spawn` (Suspected)

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, usability (score 1): a forked attempt shown as `spawn` after a reconnect (suspected).
- **Found:** 2026-10-27, by Grok's review of M2.5.4a (by reading; not executed). The agent
  sends `Started` before the process exists, with `spawn`, and a second `Started` with
  `fork` once a fork server has forked it (`Done::Spawned` in
  `crates/schedr-agent/src/agent.rs`). That second message is sent only while the master
  link is up (`if forked && let Some((to_master, _)) = &link`); when it is down, it is
  skipped, and the `Register` sent on reconnecting carries the attempt's journal state but no
  start method (`journal_entries`).
- **Effect:** the attempt shows `start_method: spawn` in the attempts API although it was
  forked; nothing else (the start-time metric is the agent's own and counts `fork`).
- **To confirm:** an agent test that forks an attempt while disconnected, then reconnects,
  and checks the methods the master gets. **A fix:** keep the method in the journal record
  (`JournalRecord::Running` with the process identity) and send it with the journal entries on
  `Register`, or send `Started{fork}` again on reconnecting.

## B4: `runs trigger` in a roles integration test got no result once

- **Rating:** severity **low**, probability **rare**, tests (score 1): one test run got no result once (likely B6, fixed).
- **Seen:** 2026-10-22, the first `make test-integration` of M2.3:
  `roles::a_worker_that_never_comes_back_is_lost_and_stays_listed` panicked in

  usual 12 s.
- **Not reproduced** in the two runs right after (53/53 passed each time). Postgres had just

- **2026-10-23:** the role tests now keep every failed or slow (over 2 s) CLI call's stderr,
  and the system's I/O stall, in their failure messages. Most likely B6 (fixed the same day:
  a 7–8 s Postgres stall after a rebuild, and the master declaring live workers lost during
  it; the trigger's CLI waits 30 s for the master's decision, and the run took 35 s instead
  of 12 s, as in B6's stalls), but unproven: no test reproduces it.

  it after a few weeks of clean `make check` runs.
